question: How many banks were nationalised by the Union Government of India in the year 1980?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Six__**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• Six __banks were nationalised by the Union Government of India in 15th April 1980.
 
• Nationalization is the transfer of ownership and management of an undertaking from private hands to the states.
 
• Banks were nationalized in India through an ordinance passed in the year 1969.
 
• Indira Gandhi was the prime minister who nationalized banks in India.
 
• The first nationalization of banks took place on 19th July 1969.
 __
 
• 14 banks were nationalized in 1969.
 
• It was based on the banks whose deposit exceeds Rs. 50 crores.
 
 
 
• The second time the government nationalized banks on 15th April 1980.
 
 
• 6 banks were nationalized in 1980.
 
• It was based on the banks whose deposit exceeds Rs. 200 crores
 
 
 
• **Six banks in are**:
 
 
• Andhra Bank: Now part of Union Bank of India
 
• Corporation Bank: Now part of Union Bank of India
 
• New Bank of India: Now part of Punjab National Bank
 
• Oriental Bank of Commerce: Now part of Punjab National Bank
 
• Punjab and Sind Bank: Nationalized in 1980
 
• Vijaya Bank: Now Bank of Baroda.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] Mistake Points__

 
• Most of the nationalized banks in India are also referred to as 'public sector banks'.
 
• After the merger of many banks, currently there are a total of 12 public sector banks in India including the State Bank of India (based on the RBI official website).
